low.label: Company's common economic interest in WhiteHawk OpCo

low.label: Required return on a non-operated gas royalty
low.rationale: No capex and no operating cost, but full commodity exposure, a single-basin pair, a first-year public company with a restated FY2025 and identified material weaknesses, and no declared dividend policy. low.label: Net annual decline in attributable producing CAFD
low.rationale: A perpetuity declining at d consumes total volume P/d, so the decline rate is what ties this component to a finite reserve book. Proved developed producing reserves of 178,544 MMcfe against pro forma annual production of 24,548 MMcfe give a 7.27-year producing life and d = 13.75%; against Q1 2026 annualised production of 23,459 MMcfe the life is 7.61 years and d = 13.14%. The band spans those two computed values. Anything shallower reaches into the non-producing and undeveloped volumes that component 2 already counts, or into unbooked acreage that no filed reserve report supports. Observed pro forma volumes fell 4.4% (67,255 to 64,270 Mcfe/d), the difference being new wells converting inventory into production -- value credited in component 2, not here.

components.evidence: Pro forma Cash Available for Distribution of $36.317m for FY2025 and $9.959m for Q1 2026, from the 424B4 reconciliation. CAFD is defined and reconciled after cash interest expense, cash taxes and cash preferred dividends, so it is an equity-level cash flow and net debt and the mezzanine preferred are deliberately not subtracted again. The Company's economic interest in WhiteHawk OpCo is applied before the per-share division so that the 14.0% held by Continuing Equity Owners is never counted as Class A value. The decline rate is bounded by the 178,544 MMcfe proved developed producing reserve book.
components.scenario_assumptions: Owner-cash leg of component_owner_cash_and_unit_nav. Declining perpetuity on attributable CAFD, with the decline rate pinned to the producing reserve life so the component cannot capitalise volume it does not own.
components.tax_and_realization_adjustments: CAFD is taken at the OpCo level and multiplied by the Company's economic interest before the per-share division. No deduction for net debt or preferred, which CAFD already services. No addition for reinvestment of retained cash into further royalty acquisitions.
components.falsifier: The first 10-Q reports net production above 67,255 Mcfe/d, implying a producing decline shallower than the 13.14%-13.75% band derived from the reserve report; or the FY2026 reserve report raises PV-10 above $500m against the $293.690m booked here; or a declared dividend sets an annualised Class A rate above $1.30 per share, which no sustainable distribution consistent with this decline band supports.

low.label: Net undeveloped reserves behind the location inventory
low.rationale: Net locations x basin-typical EUR. A net location is already gross locations scaled by net revenue interest, so multiplying by a gross per-well EUR gives net volume. Basin-weighted rather than uniform because Mid-Continent is 50% of the net count (14.1 of 28.0) on 9,314 ft laterals against Appalachia's 13,246 ft and far lower EUR per foot: a uniform rate overstates the book by roughly 40%. Bands use 2.0-2.7 Bcfe per 1,000 ft in Appalachia, 2.2-2.8 in Haynesville and 0.6-1.2 in Mid-Continent and Other. This is the largest single estimate in the contract and the one a third-party type-curve study would replace.

low.label: Share of the blended PV-10 unit value realised on undeveloped volumes
low.rationale: PV-10 of $293.690m spread over 206,473 MMcfe is $1.422 per Mcfe, but that blended rate is dominated by the 178,544 MMcfe already producing, which sit earliest in the discount schedule. The inventory is a 35-58 year drilling programme -- 8,783 gross locations at the 126-198 wells/yr implied by WhiteHawk's disclosed interest in 18% of new Appalachian and Haynesville wells -- so the average location is discounted over decades and is worth a small fraction of the blended rate. A royalty owner funds none of the development cost, so the haircut is timing and operator pace only, never capital. The band is deliberately deep: crediting this inventory at anything near the producing rate would be the routed profile's third failure mode, remote options treated as contracted cash.

low.label: Company's common economic interest in WhiteHawk OpCo
low.rationale: Same ownership arithmetic as the producing component: 86.0% today, 82.1% if the 1,250,000 earnout OpCo Interests are issued. Applied before the per-share division so the Continuing Equity Owners' 14.0% is never counted as Class A value.

low.label: Senior claims charged against this component
low.rationale: Explicitly zero, not omitted. Net debt of $64.463m ($75.000m less $10.537m cash) and the $30.643m Series B preferred are serviced inside Cash Available for Distribution, which is struck after cash interest expense and cash preferred dividends and drives the producing component. Deducting the principal here as well would charge the same claims twice -- the routed profile's 'operating cash flow and NAV counted twice' failure mode.

components.label: Finite capital-allocation value from retained CAFD and external royalty acquisitions
components.ownership_claim: Class A holders participate in the excess value, if any, created when WhiteHawk retains cash or raises capital to acquire additional mineral and royalty interests.

base.label: Net NPV created per acquisition dollar
Capital-allocation value per Class A share

components.evidence: WhiteHawk has completed eight acquisitions since inception and states that cash flow not used for dividends may be used for acquisitions meeting its criteria or to maintain a conservative capital structure. This supports a non-zero framework, not the assumed 15% net NPV creation rate.
components.scenario_assumptions: Base: 25% retention, $50m/year external capacity, 10-year finite horizon, and 15% net NPV created per acquisition dollar.
components.falsifier: Future acquisitions fail to create positive net present value per Class A share after all financing and dilution, or deployment cannot reach the assumed capacity.

components.label: Dated development timing and recurring-CAFD reconciliation to the proved-reserve floor
components.ownership_claim: Not a separate asset: this is the disclosed adjustment from the legacy reserve-contract timing convention to the dated inventory schedule and recurring CAFD view.
components.evidence: The base starts with the $8.7614/share legacy proved-reserve floor. It replaces the 17% inventory realisation factor with a dated 411 TIL/year development schedule, a +$5.232/share inventory uplift, and replaces the legacy owner-cash run rate with $22.717m recurring attributable CAFD, a -$2.0215/share production adjustment; net bridge +$3.2105/share.
components.scenario_assumptions: Base dates development through 2035. High holds the gross timing uplift and no recurring-CAFD reset; low retains the legacy reserve contract.
components.falsifier: Tract-level operator development data fails to support the dated 411 TIL/year schedule, or recurring CAFD differs materially from the stated normalization.

low.label: Net undeveloped reserves behind the location inventory
low.rationale: Net locations x basin-typical EUR. A net location is already gross locations scaled by net revenue interest, so multiplying by a gross per-well EUR gives net volume. Basin-weighted rather than uniform because Mid-Continent is 50% of the net count (14.1 of 28.0) on 9,314 ft laterals against Appalachia's 13,246 ft and far lower EUR per foot: a uniform rate overstates the book by roughly 40%. Bands use 2.0-2.7 Bcfe per 1,000 ft in Appalachia, 2.2-2.8 in Haynesville and 0.6-1.2 in Mid-Continent and Other. This is the largest single estimate in the contract and the one a third-party type-curve study would replace.

low.label: Share of the blended PV-10 unit value realised on undeveloped volumes
low.rationale: PV-10 of $293.690m spread over 206,473 MMcfe is $1.422 per Mcfe, but that blended rate is dominated by the 178,544 MMcfe already producing, which sit earliest in the discount schedule. The inventory is a 35-58 year drilling programme -- 8,783 gross locations at the 126-198 wells/yr implied by WhiteHawk's disclosed interest in 18% of new Appalachian and Haynesville wells -- so the average location is discounted over decades and is worth a small fraction of the blended rate. A royalty owner funds none of the development cost, so the haircut is timing and operator pace only, never capital. The band is deliberately deep: crediting this inventory at anything near the producing rate would be the routed profile's third failure mode, remote options treated as contracted cash.

low.label: Company's common economic interest in WhiteHawk OpCo

change_control.rule: A source fact is locked. Every assumption change requires a reason, author, timestamp, and before/after value.

options.label: Finite capital-allocation value from retained CAFD and external royalty acquisitions
options.probability_and_timing: Base assumes 25% of existing PDP CAFD is retained, $50m of annual external-acquisition capacity for 10 years, and 15% net NPV created per acquisition dollar after financing, tax, and dilution. Low gives no premium; high assumes 40% retention, $100m/year capacity, and 25% net NPV per dollar.
options.falsifier: Actual acquisition cohorts fail to create positive per-share NPV after financing and dilution, or management cannot source the assumed annual deployment capacity.
options.overlap_control: Only excess NPV on future acquisitions is credited. The purchase price and cash flows of the existing reserve book are already valued in the PDP and inventory components.

optionality.rule: Every option requires a beneficiary, probability, timing, remaining capital, failure case, and non-overlap control; absence of option value must be explicit rather than unvalued.

committee.strongest_dissent: PV-10 is an accounting floor, not intrinsic value: a trailing-twelve-month deck, a fixed 10% discount rate regardless of asset quality, and proved reserves only. Appalachian mineral packages transact above PV-10 for exactly those reasons, and WhiteHawk's operators are the best-capitalised in the basin. If 2.5x-3.0x PV-10 is where this asset class actually clears, my multiple measures the conservatism of a convention rather than an overvaluation. The packet still cannot test this, and after two rounds and a restored filing that is now a statement about the workspace rather than the company: we hold no comparable-transaction evidence for any mineral package.
unresolved_items: Arms-length transaction comparables for Marcellus and Haynesville mineral and royalty packages, expressed as a multiple of PV-10 and as dollars per net royalty acre. Established across two committee rounds as absent from the workspace entirely, not merely from this filing.

Operator development schedules against WhiteHawk's specific acreage: permits, rig allocation and announced 2027 capital budgets for EQT, Antero, Range and CNX. That would convert the realisation haircut from a judgment into a dated conversion schedule.

The actual swap schedule: notional volumes, strikes and tenor. The covenant sets the minimum hedged fraction but not the price, and the pro forma $16.052m derivative gain implies the existing book is materially in the money at the old deck. Without strikes I cannot tell whether the hedge floors CAFD near the modelled run-rate or well below it.
committee.next_action: Owner records decision, sizing, and a direct response to the strongest dissent.

method_fit.label: Scarce assets, royalties, and optionality
applicability_tests: The security owns a legally enforceable economic claim on scarce assets or royalties.
Material value is omitted or poorly represented by current GAAP earnings.
Asset quantities, ownership, overlap, timing, and remaining capital can be reconciled.
Comparable values can be adjusted for location, quality, control, liquidity, and realization time.
failure_modes: gross asset value mistaken for shareholder value
operating cash flow and NAV counted twice
remote options treated as contracted cash

validation_cohort.purpose: Test depletion, commodity exposure, finite reserves, and royalty-unit reconciliation.
Test tangible capital, credit losses, funding, regulation, and excess-capital realization.
Test owner earnings, capital-light reinvestment, cyclicality, and buyback value creation.
Test normalized margins, industry supply response, replacement cost, and reinvestment timing.
Test product concentration, pipeline probabilities, patent cliffs, and catalyst timing.

method_fit.rule: Use one primary method and no more than two corroborating methods; irrelevant methods and personas remain silent.

outcomes.weighting_rule: Do not change a persona's relevance within a power zone until at least 20 attributable, dividend-aware outcomes exist there; never reweight automatically.
